Un engine es un grupo selecto de cartas: An engine is a select group of cards from an archetype that gets splashed (teched in) into decks of other archetypes: Bystial, Horus, Sky Striker with Engage! and Widow Anchor... Here you can see which ones are used today in each mode, how much, and which cards make them up. Tap a card to see its effect and how the engine works. Standalone cards that almost everyone plays (hand traps, Pot of Greed...) are not engines: they're staples and are listed separately, at the end.
<p>Qué mazos juegan cada engine: en TCG,:
Which decks play each engine: in TCG, OCG and Genesys it comes from YuGiOh Meta's tags on recent tournament decks; in Duel Links, from Duel Links Meta's engines (a deck counts when it has at least half of the cards that identify the engine).

There are two kinds of engine. Those defined by name (The Fallen & The Virtuous, Bystial, Ars Magna, K9, Kashtira, Sinful Spoils) are always counted: a deck plays them when it has at least 2 of their cards (1 for Ars Magna), and if they're barely used they appear below with their real number. Every engine defined by YuGiOh Meta and Duel Links Meta is counted, even if it sees little play: the ones played by 5 or more decks and 1% or more are shown at the top, and under «More engines» the rest with their real number. The others are groups of cards that show up together (each in 60% or more of the other's decks) in at least 3 archetypes, or engines from Duel Links Meta and YuGiOh Meta with their archetype; in that case only the decks that splash them count, and they are measured against each other.

"How it works" lists the engine's cards with their effect text, plus how many decks and archetypes play it. It's sample data, not an opinion.
